## Phase: 66 - Signal-Richness Falsification + Scorer Park + audit-log Disposition

### The signal-richness gate FAILED — scorer is NOT-SCOREABLE, 2 of 4 blockers are structural
from: [[decision:park-enforcement-scorer-signal-insufficient]]
retrieved: 2026-05-29

- Measured against the live enforcement.log: only 11 new-format (`schema_version=1`) records — ALL from one hook (dev-wiki-scope-check), ZERO action-changing `block` firings, all `phase:"65"` intra-phase self-traffic. The 253 enforce-loop + 23 block records that LOOK like signal are PRE-instrumentation LEGACY format (no schema_version, no phase) — NOT what a scorer consumes. The new/old discriminator is `schema_version` (NOT `phase`; legacy lacks both).
- Unbuildable for 4 stacked reasons, 3 not fixed by time: (1) volume [time fixes]; (2) skew — 0 blocks, 1/6 hooks; (3) REPRESENTATIVENESS [structural] — the log lives in the kit's OWN .dev-wiki, sampling the maintainer editing the kit, never the consuming-project agentic work enforcement governs; (4) SCHEMA GAP [structural] — the record captures the hook's DECISION, not the agent's subsequent ACTION; "change-an-action" needs a firing→response link no field carries. Verbatim "measurement before optimization; don't optimize what you haven't measured."

### Park = a runnable probe + two named preconditions, NOT a calendar note
from: [[decision:park-enforcement-scorer-signal-insufficient]]
retrieved: 2026-05-29

- The deferral is legitimate only because it is falsifiable: `scripts/signal-richness-probe.sh` IS the gate (read-only, deterministic). Its SCOREABLE verdict — ≥2 distinct hooks AND ≥1 `block`, over schema_version-bearing records after full-`{hook,ts,action,reason}`-tuple dedup — is the trigger; green ⇒ revisit. A "come back later" that can't be expressed as a runnable check is rejected.
- Volume is NECESSARY-not-sufficient: the trigger ALSO requires the 2 structural blockers resolved first — real consuming-project provenance (point the probe at an installed project's log) AND a record schema that captures the agent's action (a precondition for ANY action-delta scorer, designed-then-reopened, not built here). NO silent scorer rebuild: the probe only counts/classifies (no ON/OFF harness run, no graded eval scenario — that = corpus-duplication, settled in [[instrument-not-score-enforcement-firing-substrate]]).

### audit-log disposition is a subtraction-test on consumer-value, NOT a broken-hook fix
from: spec phase-66 + adversarial review
retrieved: 2026-05-29

- audit-log.sh FUNCTIONS (eval-covered by 2 corpus scenarios: hook-audit-log-{write,no-file} + lifecycle-full-session-flow); it produces nothing in the kit's own repo only because the kit doesn't install project-local hooks on itself. So keep-vs-cut hinges on whether the `.nana/audit.jsonl` trail EARNS its surface — judged by its INTENDED consumer (human forensic "which model edited which file when" of an installed project), NOT by grepping for in-repo readers (there are none — only self-test.md `cat` + a harness-audit.sh path reference). If KEEP, name the human consumer explicitly so a later sweep doesn't re-flag it as dead code.
- audit-log interpolates the raw `$FILE_PATH` via `printf` (NOT the jq --arg controlled-vocab discipline the enforcement.log hardening enforced) — keep it OUT of the firing-log family / scorer input; the decision article must state how each path handles that surface. CUT reconciles ALL coupled surfaces atomically: modules.json + regenerated settings.json (via `make template`, NEVER hand-edit) + install.sh + file-lifecycle.md + README + 2 eval scenarios (dynamic count → make eval 50, no literal edit per [[eval-total-is-dynamic]]) + lifecycle-full-session-flow rewire; test_registration (bidirectional) + test_settings_template (drift) are what catch a half-done cut.

### Data-quality findings surfaced while measuring (don't expand scope to fix)
from: spec phase-66 adversarial review
retrieved: 2026-05-29

- Suspected double-emit: every multi-event new-format timestamp appears EXACTLY twice, byte-identical — could be a dev-wiki-scope-check double-call OR two same-second out-of-scope edits (indistinguishable at second resolution). Probe dedups on the full tuple AND reports the raw rate; fix ONLY if reading the hook shows a clear double-`log_firing` call (DISCOVERY), else note as caveat — NO dev-wiki-scope-check refactor.
- dev-debrief writes a DIFFERENT schema (`{event:"debrief",...}`) into the same enforcement.log — off-roster (not one of the 6 instrumented hooks). Probe CLASSIFIES it (a reported bucket), never counts it toward signal; don't choke on it. test_firing_log.sh already proves all 6 hooks emit when fired, so the 5/6 historical silence = "no cause to fire," not a broken write path.
